title: Concurrent OpenCode sessions and worktree coordination
objective: Provide a clear, resource-aware workflow for multiple OpenCode sessions, parallel Git worktrees, and future agentic loops without treating nested VMs as a prerequisite.

acceptance_criteria.text: README and VM architecture explain when to use one profile, multiple sessions on one guest, separate profiles/worktrees, a common parent mount, and nested self-testing, with implemented/manual/unavailable status clearly labeled.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: README.md ‘Choosing sessions, workspaces, and branches’ and docs/vm-architecture.md ‘Sessions, worktrees, and parallel agents’ record the choice matrix and current limits.

acceptance_criteria.text: Multiple concurrent OpenCode sessions on one VM profile have independent temporary browser-auth listeners and no shared-port collision; shared workspace and guest-state risks are explicit.
An operator can select a distinct Git worktree/project directory per OpenCode session within one deliberately selected workspace, without accidentally exposing paths outside the mounted parent.

A future multi-agent/agentic-loop supervisor defines per-agent worktree/session ownership, resource limits, cancellation, retries, result integration, and cleanup; it does not require a nested VM for ordinary parallel work.

Regression and owner-host tests verify concurrent TUI/auth sessions, per-session workspace selection, worktree isolation, and clean cancellation/cleanup; nested VM is required only for recursive Little Mester self-testing and has separate depth/isolation gates.

needed: On a supported KVM host, open two direct guest OpenCode sessions concurrently on one profile; verify both remain usable and do not edit the same worktree.
Run two browser-auth sessions concurrently on one profile; verify per-session host and guest loopback ports, independent tokens/cleanup, and no listener adoption or replacement.
Implement and test a per-session worktree/cwd selector constrained to the single mounted parent; prove sibling paths outside that parent are unavailable.
Specify and test supervisor ownership, resource budgets, cancellation, retries, result handoff, and cleanup before claiming multi-agent loops.
created: README.md and docs/vm-architecture.md: session/profile/worktree/nesting choice matrix and explicit current limits.
tests/test_vm_browser_bridge.py: per-session environment-selected host port, no-guess behavior without a session port, and simultaneous independent loopback listeners.
cases: 2026-10-30 implementation follow-up: static browser port 19533 was removed from the normal launcher/client path. Each auth run binds an ephemeral host-loopback bridge and chooses a guest-loopback reverse-forward port; the guest client receives that session port. Local browser-bridge tests pass 13/13 within the full VM Python suite 47/47. This proves port-selection logic, not concurrent live SSH/TUI acceptance; Bats, ShellCheck, and KVM host verification remain unavailable/pending. README.md and docs/vm-architecture.md describe separate profiles/worktrees and mark session cwd selection and agent-loop supervision as future work.
